09:45 Local Time, 08:45 GMT, 14:15 IST: Hello and a warm welcome to our live coverage of the second game of the 5-match ODI series between Ireland and Afghanistan. The first game was abandoned due to rain without even the toss taking place. The good news is that better weather is expected through the course of the day at this venue. When it comes to the head-to-head in ODIs between these two sides, Afghanistan have the edge with 18 wins while Ireland have 13 wins out of 33 games.

The washout in the first ODI has shut the door on Ireland in terms of direct qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup. They will need to fight it out in the qualifiers to reach the mega event. Afghanistan, meanwhile, are in a strong position to directly qualify for the mega event. It’s an important series as both teams will be eager to build momentum.

Both teams have strong players across all departments. Afghanistan’s key strengths are their world class spinners and explosive opening batters. On the other hand, Ireland have experience in their batting lineup and their seamers have the ability to exploit the useful conditions on offer. It should be a fascinating contest! Toss and team lineups will be announced shortly...

So, we will have to wait another half an hour or so.

10:44 Local Time, 09:44 GMT, 15:14 IST: The next inspection is at 11.15am local. There are some wet patches on the outfield that need attention. The waiting game continues...

Rahmat Shah | Afghanistan captain: (On batting first) Yeah, I'm happy with that. (On the surface and a good score here?) I think we are not thinking about a specific number. We just build the partnerships as much as possible. (On getting the full-time captaincy and his vision now?) I just give the positive thing to the players. They play their natural game, and we want to try our best. We have three spinners and three fast bowlers.

Pitch Report | Ed Joyce: Ireland have won the toss and are bowling first, probably because of the overhead conditions and they don't know how this pitch is going to play. Just having a quick look at the pitch, considering the amount of rain we've had over the last couple of days, it's actually pretty dry. So I don't think Afghanistan are going to be too unhappy about batting first on this and then using their spinners in the second half to see if there's a bit of turn in it, because I think there probably will be a bit of turn. There are some bare patches as well if we look around. So, yeah, all in all, not much grass in it, pretty dry, and I do think there'll be a bit of turn in the second innings.
